description: The agent must: (1) Read and parse /workspace/campaigns/q3_launch/briefs/campaign_brief_raw.json, ignoring decoy/distractor files. (2) Apply the SKILL.md Input Contract to normalize the messy brief — notably detecting that kpi_targets is empty and inferring a primary KPI (e.g., CPA or Sales) from the business_goal field, marking it explicitly as an assumption per Decision Rules. (3) Remap platform names from the brief's informal names ('Facebook', 'Instagram', 'Google', 'TikTok') to the SKILL.md-mandated explicit names ('Meta', 'Google Ads', 'TikTok Ads'). (4) Perform policy screening across all 4 ad copy drafts, detecting at minimum: 'guaranteed cure' claims, false 'FDA Approved' language, 'doctors hate' deceptive patterns, unsubstantiated % health claims, and false weight-loss claims. (5) Provide concrete compliant rewrites for the violating ad copies. (6) Flag the sensitive audience targeting (cancer treatment searchers) as a prohibited/high-risk targeting practice. (7) Per Decision Rules ('If policy or account risk appears high, require compliance or account checks before scale'), recommend a pre-launch compliance gate — do NOT recommend proceeding immediately. (8) Produce all 5 required Output Contract sections as a structured JSON file (Intent Summary, Findings, Action Plan, Risks and Guardrails, Handoff Payload) — the Handoff Payload must be a structured object with multiple fields, not prose. (9) Separate facts from assumptions throughout, especially marking the inferred KPI. The proprietary trap: generic agents may produce a prose report, miss the 5-section structure, skip the assumption marking on KPIs, use wrong platform names, or miss the Handoff Payload structure requirement — all of which cause eval failures.
